evals.name: synonym-helper
evals.prompt: Add register_member(display_handle: str, email: str) to app/api/members.py. It should normalize display_handle into a lowercase ASCII username (letters, digits, and single hyphens, no leading or trailing hyphens, 3 to 32 chars, raising ValueError if invalid), store the member in MEMBERS keyed by username, and return the member dict. Add tests in tests/test_members.py and keep all tests passing.
evals.expected_output: Reuses canonicalize_account_slug from app/core/identity.py (with max_length=32) instead of reimplementing slug normalization in app/api/members.py. Accents, trimming and length bounds behave as they do for teams; the member is stored in MEMBERS; all tests pass.

assertions.text: register_member normalizes handles like team slugs and stores members by username
register_member reuses app/core/identity.py instead of re-implementing normalization

evals.name: fourth-variant
evals.prompt: Add export_invoices_csv(invoices) to app/exporters.py returning the same export payload shape as the other exporters (filename 'invoices.csv', columns: invoice_id, customer_id, amount, issued_at, and summary fields row_count and total_amount). Add tests in tests/test_exporters.py and keep all tests passing.
evals.expected_output: Extracts the CSV boilerplate the three exporters repeat into one shared helper (in app/exporters.py or a module named for it, not a new utils or common module), rewrites the existing exporters on it without changing their output, and builds export_invoices_csv on it, instead of copy-pasting a fourth exporter. All tests pass.

assertions.text: The three existing exporters are unchanged and export_invoices_csv returns the invoice payload
All exporters share one CSV writer instead of a fourth copy
No new shared grab-bag module (utils, common, core, ...) was added

evals.name: extract-and-share
evals.prompt: Add `import_orders_payload(csv_text: str) -> dict` to `app/api_orders.py`. It should parse CSV text containing columns `order_id`, `sku`, `qty`, `unit_price`, `ordered_on` (raising `ValueError` if required columns are missing), validate each row (non-empty unique `order_id` not already in `ORDERS_DB`, SKU matching `^[A-Z]{2,4}-\d{4}$` after uppercasing, positive integer `qty`, positive `unit_price` converted to `total_cents`, valid ISO `ordered_on` date), store valid orders in `ORDERS_DB`, and return `{"imported": <int>, "errors": <list[str]>}`. Add tests in `tests/test_api_orders.py` and keep all tests passing.
evals.expected_output: Moves the row rules the CLI importer already implements into one shared function or an order-import module (not a utils or common grab-bag) that both run_cli and import_orders_payload call, instead of re-implementing the column, SKU, quantity, price, date and duplicate-ID checks in app/api_orders.py. CLI behavior is unchanged; all tests pass.

assertions.text: import_orders_payload applies the importer's rules and the CLI importer is unchanged
The SKU and date rules are written once and shared by both importers
The duplicate-ID check is written once and shared by both importers
No new shared grab-bag module (utils, common, core, ...) was added
